rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose way to indicate going to or being at one's home.

example.jyutping: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 faan1 uk1 kei2

rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for one's own house or one's parental home.

example.english: I'm not going home for dinner tonight.
example.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 maan5 m4 faan1 uk1 kei2 sik6 faan6

rows.note: Use this more conceptual or written-leaning word for the family home or a home as a place of emotional belonging.

example.english: To me, home is the place where I feel most at ease.
example.traditional: 對我嚟講，家就係最安心嘅地方。
example.jyutping: deoi3 ngo5 lei4 gong2 gaa1 zau6 hai6 zeoi3 on1 sam1 ge3 dei6 fong1

rows.note: Use this for one's native land or hometown rather than the house one currently lives in.

example.english: When I retire, I'll go back home to live in my hometown.
example.jyutping: ngo5 jat1 teoi3 jau1 zau6 faan1 gaa1 hoeng1 zyu6

rows.note: Use this for a refuge or asylum, not for an ordinary private home.

example.english: This shelter gives homeless people a temporary home.
example.traditional: 呢間收容所俾無家可歸嘅人一個暫時嘅家。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 sau1 jung4 so2 bei2 mou4 gaa1 ho2 gwai1 ge3 jan4 jat1 go3 zaam6 si4 ge3 gaa1
